original_question: In the Post Correspondence Problem, an instance (h, g) is a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word u and every pair of distinct letters a and b, the comparabilities h(ua) ⊲⊳ g(ua) and h(ub) ⊲⊳ g(ub) together imply h(u) = g(u). Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable for this class of instances?
target_in_paper: Question 3.5.05.1: Is PCP decidable for unique equality continuation instances?

refined_question: Let Σ and Δ be finite alphabets, and let h, g: Σ* -> Δ* be morphisms. Recall that the Post Correspondence Problem asks whether there exists a nonempty word x in Σ* such that h(x) = g(x). Call two words y, z in Δ* comparable if one is a prefix of the other. An instance (h, g) is called a unique equality continuation instance if, for every word u in Σ* and every pair of distinct letters a, b in Σ, the comparabilities of h(ua) with g(ua) and of h(ub) with g(ub) together imply h(u) = g(u). Is the Post Correspondence Problem decidable when restricted to unique equality continuation instances?
justification: The paper states this question explicitly in Section 3.5, immediately after introducing the comparability relation and the definition of a unique equality continuation instance. Your draft is therefore very close to the paper-faithful target already. The refinement only makes explicit the standard PCP data and quantifiers that the paper leaves implicit in its brief survey-style wording. I did not broaden the question to the adjacent Question 3.5.05.2, because that is a different decision problem.
